title: Advanced MPC and moving horizon estimation
text: Moving horizon estimation (MHE) estimates state solving, every sample, least-squares problem window last N measurements:  \min \|x_s - \bar x_s\|^2_{P_s^{-1}} + \sum_{j=s}^{T-1} \|w_j\|^2_{Q_n^{-1}} + \sum_{j=s}^{T} \|y_j - C x_j - D u_j\|^2_{R_n^{-1}}  subject model bounds states process noise. first term, arrival cost, summarizes data window. prior mean propagated previous MHE estimate prior covariance follows Kalman filter recursion. active constraints MHE equals Kalman filter exactly, tests verify. MHE Kalman filter: states physical bounds (concentration negative), bounds enter estimate. price one QP per sample, growing window length. window’s QP starts previous solution shifted one sample, primal dual (warm_start = TRUE, default). estimates change; solver work :
code: set.seed(5) sys <- ctrl_ss(0.95, 1, 1, dt = 1) Tn <- 80 x <- 0.05 xs <- numeric(Tn) y <- numeric(Tn) for (k in 1:Tn) {   xs[k] <- x   y[k] <- x + rnorm(1, sd = 0.3)   x <- max(0, 0.95 * x + rnorm(1, sd = 0.02)) } kf <- ctrl_kalman_filter(sys, y, Qn = 4e-4, Rn = 0.09, x0 = 0, P0 = 1) mhe <- ctrl_mhe(sys, horizon = 10, Qn = 4e-4, Rn = 0.09, x0 = 0, P0 = 1, x_min = 0) est <- ctrl_mhe_run(mhe, y) c(kalman_min = min(kf$filtered), mhe_min = min(est$estimates)) #>    kalman_min       mhe_min  #> -2.331457e-01 -1.610433e-17 c(kalman_rmse = sqrt(mean((kf$filtered[, 1] - xs)^2)),   mhe_rmse = sqrt(mean((est$estimates[, 1] - xs)^2))) #> kalman_rmse    mhe_rmse  #>  0.05471087  0.03395546 cold <- ctrl_mhe_run(mhe, y, warm_start = FALSE) c(max_difference = max(abs(cold$estimates - est$estimates)),   iterations_cold = sum(cold$iterations), iterations_warm = sum(est$iterations)) #>  max_difference iterations_cold iterations_warm  #>               0            5400            5625 df <- data.frame(k = rep(1:Tn, 3),                  value = c(xs, kf$filtered[, 1], est$estimates[, 1]),                  series = rep(c("true", "Kalman", "MHE"), each = Tn)) ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(k, value, color = series)) +   ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +   ggplot2::theme_bw()

title: Stability, controllability and matrix equations
text: continuous time model asymptotically stable every pole negative real part; discrete time model every pole lies strictly inside unit circle. Poles boundary need care: simple pole imaginary axis gives marginally stable model, repeated boundary pole nontrivial Jordan block grows without bound. ctrl_stability() distinguishes cases tolerance scaled size : ctrl_damp() lists natural frequencies damping ratios (discrete models equivalent continuous poles \log(z)/T):

text: x_{k+1} = x_k + B u_k + G w_k, y_k = C x_k + D u_k + v_k noise covariances Q_n R_n, ctrl_kalman() returns steady-state gains. conventions stated precisely packages differ: P prior (predicted) covariance P_{k|k-1}; M measurement update gain, \hat x_{k|k} = \hat x_{k|k-1} + M (y_k - C \hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k); L one-step predictor gain (L = without cross covariance); Z posterior covariance P_{k|k}. "tustin": bilinear transformation \(s = \frac{2}{T}\frac{z-1}{z+1}\), optionally prewarped frequency response matches exactly prewarp rad per time unit. "matched": matched pole-zero mapping \(z = e^{sT}\) SISO models, zeros infinity mapped \(z = -1\) (one, result stays strictly proper original ) gain matched DC (s = j/T pole zero 0). Matrix exponentials use expm::expm() (scaling squaring Pade approximation).

title: H2 optimal output-feedback synthesis — ctrl_h2syn
text: Assumptions (checked; violations raise errors): \(D_{11} = 0\) (closed-loop H2 norm finite), \(D_{12}\) full column rank, \(D_{21}\) full row rank, \((, B_2)\) stabilizable, \((C_2, )\) detectable, invariant zeros \((, B_2, C_1, D_{12})\) \((, B_1, C_2, D_{21})\) subsystems imaginary axis (detected Riccati failures). Algorithm. Two Riccati equations (Zhou, Doyle Glover, 1996, Theorem 14.7): \(X_2\) = ctrl_care(, B2, C1'C1, D12'D12, C1'D12), \(F_2 = -(D_{12}^\top D_{12})^{-1}(B_2^\top X_2 + D_{12}^\top C_1)\); \(Y_2\) = ctrl_care(', C2', B1 B1', D21 D21', B1 D21'), \(L_2 = -(Y_2 C_2^\top + B_1 D_{21}^\top)(D_{21} D_{21}^\top)^{-1}\); controller \(A_K = + B_2 F_2 + L_2 C_2\), \(B_K = -L_2\), \(C_K = F_2\), \(D_K = 0\) (loop shift \(D_{22} \ne 0\)). closed-loop H2 norm computed independently ctrl_norm() returned.

title: H-infinity output-feedback synthesis (experimental) — ctrl_hinfsyn
text: Scope. Continuous time , \(D_{11} = 0\), \(D_{12}\) full column rank, \(D_{21}\) full row rank, \((, B_2)\) stabilizable \((C_2, )\) detectable; arbitrary \(D_{22}\) handled loop shift. Plants \(D_{11} \ne 0\) (example mixed-sensitivity designs biproper sensitivity weight) rejected, discrete time plants. Algorithm. plant first normalized orthogonal transformations z w invertible scalings u y \(D_{12} = [0; ]\) \(D_{21} = [0, ]\) (leave H-infinity norm unchanged). given \(\gamma\), two H-infinity Riccati equations Glover Doyle (1988) solved ctrl_care() indefinite weights; \(\gamma\) feasible stabilizing solutions exist, \(X_\infty \succeq 0\), \(Y_\infty \succeq 0\) \(\rho(X_\infty Y_\infty) < \gamma^2\). central controller \(A_K = + \gamma^{-2} B_1 B_1^\top X_\infty + B_2 F_\infty + Z_\infty L_\infty (C_2 + \gamma^{-2} D_{21} B_1^\top X_\infty)\), \(B_K = -Z_\infty L_\infty\), \(C_K = F_\infty\), \(D_K = 0\), \(F_\infty = -(D_{12}^\top C_1 + B_2^\top X_\infty)\), \(L_\infty = -(B_1 D_{21}^\top + Y_\infty C_2^\top)\) \(Z_\infty = (- \gamma^{-2} Y_\infty X_\infty)^{-1}\). Certification. Every returned controller checked independently: closed loop must internally stable H-infinity norm, computed ctrl_norm() (Bruinsma-Steinbuch, different algorithm), must \(\gamma\). check fails, error raised instead returning uncertified controller. bisection stops relative tolerance tol returns controller smallest feasible \(\gamma\) found, slightly suboptimal design: central controller becomes ill-conditioned optimum.

title: Steady-state Kalman filter — ctrl_kalman
text: Discrete time conventions: P steady-state prior covariance \(P_{k|k-1}\); M measurement-update (innovation) gain \(M = P C^\top (C P C^\top + R_n)^{-1}\) used \(\hat x_{k|k} = \hat x_{k|k-1} + M (y_k - C\hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k)\); L one-step predictor gain \(L = (P C^\top + G N_n)(C P C^\top + R_n)^{-1}\) used \(\hat x_{k+1|k} = \hat x_{k|k-1} + B u_k + L(y_k - C \hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k)\); Z posterior covariance \(P_{k|k}\) (\(N_n = 0\)). continuous time, L Kalman-Bucy gain \((P C^\top + G N_n) R_n^{-1}\). Rn must positive definite: perfect (noise-free) measurements make filtering problem singular silently regularized. Qn may singular (including zero) long Riccati equation stabilizing solution; requires \((, C)\) detectable unreachable noise modes stability boundary.

title: Time-varying discrete Kalman filter and smoother — ctrl_kalman_filter
text: Conventions. x0 P0 prior mean covariance state first sample, \(\hat x_{1|0}\) \(P_{1|0}\). step first updates \(y_k\) predicts \(k + 1\): $$e_k = y_k - C \hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k, \quad S_k = C P_{k|k-1} C^\top + R_n, \quad K_k = P_{k|k-1} C^\top S_k^{-1},$$ $$\hat x_{k|k} = \hat x_{k|k-1} + K_k e_k, \quad \hat x_{k+1|k} = \hat x_{k|k} + B u_k.$$ covariance update uses Joseph form \(P_{k|k} = (- K_k C) P_{k|k-1} (- K_k C)^\top + K_k R_n K_k^\top\), keeps symmetric positive semidefinite floating point. Rows y entirely NA treated missing measurements (update skipped); partially missing rows, infinite values non-numeric data errors. ctrl_kalman_smoother() applies Rauch-Tung-Striebel backward pass filter output.
